The bundled Windows assembler binary and VICE environment are host build/test aids, not the runtime target ISA. Build: bass.bat invokes 64tass and the checked-in bass64.out reports no errors/warnings with 64tass 1.53.1515. The complete tree contains included assembly tables, build wrappers, PRG/D64 outputs, native-build sources and VICE snapshots. Usage remains unknown. Relationships: Original Commodore copyright is retained in the assembler source; no root LICENSE or blanket grant is present in the complete tree. 64tass’s notice applies to that assembler, not automatically to reconstructed Commodore code. The preserved original AmigaOS3 engine is an actual 68k C-source lineage. The SPC700 language is decode-capable with p-code still under rewrite; the 65C816 language is disassembly-oriented while its p-code is verified against exhaustive vectors. Current NES work resolves proven constant-pointer indirect jumps and bounds table-after-code jump tables by their switch window; Mega Man and Life Force rows were re-blessed, while Contra, Final Fantasy and TMNT changes remain held for owner review. Its exhaustive 65C816 vector baseline now reports 500 PASS, 8 N/A and 4 FAIL rows after isolating one named SBC (dp,X) test-vector oracle defect. The exception is guarded by tripwires that fail if the case starts passing or disappears, so it cannot mask wider regressions. Build and real-ROM gates therefore demonstrate bounded progress rather than universal correctness claims.

The shared repository is the project unit; the listings do not establish separately maintained projects. Binary-only hi-res disks and unreviewed anthology entries are not promoted by association. Source CPU: The reviewed BASIC sources target the original Apple II and include direct I/O accesses and POKE-installed 6502 speaker instructions, including LDA $C030. This establishes a 6502 implementation from embedded code and the explicit machine target, rather than from BASIC syntax alone. Target CPU: These preserved listings execute through the appropriate Apple II BASIC interpreter plus embedded 6502 instructions. No port to a new ISA or native 65816 build is established for this reviewed collection. Build: The author provides the complete plain-text Basketball, Country Drive and Tag listings and a lo-res disk image. Basketball and Country Drive use Integer BASIC; Tag uses Applesoft BASIC. No compiler is inherently required, but no listing was run or compared with disk contents. Basketball line 740 branches to nonexistent line 2550, while its listing ends with 2250; this potential exit-path defect is retained without repair or a claim of tested failure. Limitations: Static discovery only. No source was built, executed, played, hardware-tested or byte-compared; independent verification flags remain null. Runtime profiles: Basketball requires Integer BASIC and two paddle inputs PDL(0)/PDL(1). Country Drive requires Integer BASIC, paddle 0 and a paddle button, with a keyboard quick-stop option. Tag requires Applesoft BASIC and two keyboard movement-key sets. Low-resolution graphics and speaker access are explicit in all three. Exact RAM and ROM-version minima remain unspecified. ntvcm-cpm-cli-runner.status: Substantive source reviewed; independent build, runtime and equivalence untested
ntvcm-cpm-cli-runner.notes: NT Virtual CP/M Machine is a standalone C++ command-line runner for CP/M .COM tools. ntvcm.cxx loads a selected host file at guest 0x100, creates CP/M entry hooks and enters x80.cxx. README documents asm/load, Turbo Pascal, Aztec C, WordStar and many other tools; they are compatibility examples, not separately reconstructed projects. The current head has removed the former GDB/MI debugger-host mode, so it is not advertised as a current capability. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: be598f65c1b649f5250dcd6d8fef266b1b86413e. An emulator with native CP/M BDOS/file and console translation, an 8080/Z80 trace disassembler and optional per-PC CSV profiling. It executes original instructions and synthesizes BDOS/BIOS hooks rather than booting a CP/M disk or requiring an original ROM. Host fopen/fread/fwrite implement FCB file operations. Original guest tools must be supplied with their own overlays/data; this record is the runner, not a full disk/hardware emulator or compiler reconstruction. x80.cxx and README explicitly implement Z80 with optional -8 8080 mode, making both guest source ISAs. CP/M 2.2 is the main guest API, supplemented by selected CP/M 3 and nonstandard services. README excludes BIOS disk-layout access, undocumented 8080 instructions and precise cycle accuracy. Recent commits distinguish optional Z80 R/MEMPTR accuracy and unattached I/O gaps; upstream validation reports do not establish universal instruction/hardware compatibility. msvcenv.bat explicitly selects Windows x86, x64 and ARM64 native toolchains. README documents a RISC-V Linux output runnable under RVOS and a real-mode DOS Watcom output; mwatcom.bat uses -0 with the DOS target, grounding 8086. Canonical target labels refer to these host executables, while source 8080/Z80 remains separate. RVOS’s AMD64/ARM32/etc host list does not automatically prove native ntvcm ports on every such system. Linux/macOS recipes do not establish an exhaustive ISA matrix. Native MSVC/g++ recipes and the Watcom real-mode DOS route are present. Unix release scripts default to RSS disabled; enabling RSS introduces cpp-httplib/OpenSSL dependencies, and README reports unresolved macOS RSS-enabled builds. Windows mr.bat enables RSS. A pinned-head Windows-2022 MSVC CI run succeeded and archived ntvcm.exe; the workflow contains no guest-test step. These observed upstream build results remain separate from maintainer CPU-test claims and this unrun review. All four build flags remain null: compilation, execution, gameplay and byte-equivalence are independently unverified. The real-mode DOS output and explicit host toolchain choices are preserved in target fields, but no numeric RAM or supported minimum DOS/Windows/macOS/Linux version is established. ntvdm-dos-cli-runner.status: Substantive source reviewed; independent build, runtime and equivalence untested
ntvdm-dos-cli-runner.notes: David Lee’s NT Virtual DOS Machine is an independent portable 8086/text-mode DOS runner, distinct from Microsoft’s system NTVDM component. ntvdm.cxx loads .COM and MZ/ZM .EXE files, applies relocations and runs i8086.cxx. README documents direct console/script use of MASM, Link, Microsoft C, Turbo Pascal/C, QuickBasic and other legacy tools. Original test software is included but does not become reconstructed source or separate runner records. Canonical root was absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior deduplication index. Inspected default-branch head: 0649657d912f23e60b32971d1c45653d48b440e3. Tooling combines an 8086 interpreter with partial DOS 3.00-style APIs, BIOS/text-console and selected interrupt behavior. The loader creates PSP/environment and synthetic interrupt stubs; DOS file calls use native host fopen/fread/fwrite and -r maps a host directory to C:. Original executables run without a booted DOS OS or vendor ROM in the normal path. Optional boot-sector loading does not establish a complete PC hardware emulator. The guest CPU is explicitly Intel 8086 and source_platforms=DOS; a compiler producing other target code does not change the executed guest ISA. README excludes graphics, sound and mouse and cautions that CPU/cycle fidelity is incomplete. It documents application-specific limitations such as QuickC incremental linker access to missing memory control blocks and a COBOL linker requiring 286. The 8086 capability must not be expanded to general 286/protected-mode compatibility. README explicitly lists Windows x64/ARM64, Linux x64/x32/ARM32/ARM64/RISC-V, and macOS ARM64 M1/M3. It also reports big-endian builds for 68000 via m68 and SPARC v8 via sparcos, which are emulated-runtime outputs rather than independent tests on physical legacy machines. Canonical x86, x86-64, ARM, ARM64, RISC-V and m68000 labels are retained. The pinned m68/ntvdm/mntvdm.sh recipe explicitly selects 68000 and builds ntvdm.elf using the newlib/BSP route; it assumes guest source files have been made available locally, and was not run. The SPARC-v8/Linux route through sparcos remains an explicit maintainer runtime claim in notes: no concrete ntvdm SPARC build/output recipe was identified, so SPARC is omitted from target_cpu. No cross-product guarantee across all hosts and CPUs is claimed. MSVC/g++ scripts build the C++ interpreter/runtime; Linux release links statically with OpenMP and macOS uses pthread/signed-char settings. mr.sh deliberately uses -O2 and documents a maintainer-observed g++11.4 -O3/-Ofast code-generation problem. The pinned-head Windows-2022 MSVC CI run succeeded and archived ntvdm.exe, but its workflow runs no guest regression suite. README and commit test reports remain upstream claims; no compiler, test harness or DOS guest was executed here. paratos.status: Substantive source reviewed; experimental compatibility; build and runtime independently untested
paratos.notes: ParaTos is an experimental direct runner for original Atari TOS/MiNT command-line applications. README identifies Linux and explains the system-call translation approach. gemdos/loader.c reads and endian-converts the PRG header, builds the basepage/environment, copies text/data, applies relocation fixups and appends ARGV data. paratos.c loads the named executable and enters the CPU engine directly, without an ST machine boot. A 2023 upstream commit explicitly added OSX support, and current Apple-specific executable-path and byte-order code remains present; this refines the earlier discovery’s Linux-only evidence without asserting that a modern macOS build was tested. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot 9d43e70bce3ed4f82ee43e35375994332fc2ac4b, non-truncated tree with 106 entries. Tooling with CPU-emulator and GEMDOS/API-reimplementation capabilities. ParaTos invokes Musashi to execute original 68k instructions and dispatches guest trap calls to native host implementations; gemdos/path.c converts TOS/MiNT filenames to POSIX paths, with case-insensitive and 8.3-name lookup. It accepts U: and rejects other drive-letter mappings in this snapshot. This is not a compiler translating the guest to host source and not an ST hardware emulator. README restricts the intended programs to clean command-line tools avoiding direct hardware and OS trap-vector patching. The implementation is incomplete, and minimal BIOS/AES/VDI paths do not establish a desktop compatibility environment. The historical binaries are 68k TOS/MiNT programs. README calls the bundled engine m68000, while current paratos.c explicitly chooses M68K_CPU_TYPE_68020 for execution and disassembly. source_cpu records the documented 68000 family entry point and the concrete 68020 guest engine rather than silently retaining the discovery’s m68000-only description. paratos.c states that the FPU is not emulated. The alternative branch reserves 512 MiB and is not an identified support matrix for every 32-bit or ARM host; no additional CPU is inferred from that fallback, C11, Clang or macOS. memory.i explicitly assumes host unaligned loads/stores. run68x-human68k-cli-runner.notes: run68x is the maintained Human68k CUI emulator derived from run68. The README names rururutan/run68 and several run68mac forks as origins. The current C implementation has its own executable loader, 68000 interpreter, debugger and Human68k-compatible services. One family is counted; original run68 and the linked macOS variants are lineage references, not additional discoveries. Inspected default-branch head: fc28826dd795b1f0a3241f0b03fe2353e12e7233. Modern tooling executes original Human68k .X and raw .R programs from argv, using host files and the existing terminal. load.c reads the HU header, performs relocation and initializes BSS; run68.c builds a PSP and enters the interpreter. DOS calls, IOCS and FE floating-point helpers are implemented in host C. The initialized HUMAN.SYS name represents a synthetic PSP, not a required OS image. The inspected direct-run path needs no original ROM or booted Human68k. The guest is the Motorola 68000 instruction set, explicitly retained even when the -himem option expands addressability. The interpreter dispatches instructions by their upper nibble. High memory is a non-hardware-compatible extension and does not imply a 68020/68060 guest. The X-file loader rejects bound executables; partial DOS/IOCS and graphics-related stubs do not establish arbitrary X68000 application or hardware compatibility. The host executable has explicit Windows x64 evidence in README and the win-x64 release workflow, so target_cpu is x86-64. Windows and Ubuntu under WSL are maintainer-confirmed build environments. Linux and macOS also have configured CMake workflows with successful runs for this exact head. No host ISA is inferred from macos-latest, ubuntu-latest, C source, or the emulated 68000. NetBSD/MSYS/Emscripten conditionals are retained as portability hints, not verified runtime ports. CMake >=3.22 builds C11 source, with shlwapi on Windows and libm plus optional/default iconv on non-MSVC routes. README confirms Visual Studio 2022 x64 and WSL Ubuntu 24.04. At the pinned head GitHub reports successful Windows/Linux CMake, macOS CMake, win-x64 release and CodeQL runs. These are observed upstream results, not independent builds. CMake contains no registered tests; a successful ctest workflow step cannot prove guest compatibility. All four build flags remain null: compilation, execution, gameplay and byte-equivalence are independently unverified. No explicit minimum host OS version, CPU generation, RAM or terminal requirement was established for the shipped outputs. VS2022 and Ubuntu 24.04 are build/test environments, and the 16–768 MiB -himem values describe emulated guest memory, not host minimum RAM. runtime_profiles remains empty. Original disk, extracted resources and generated C are omitted and must be supplied/regenerated. Decryptor byte-exact claims concern a protection-analysis oracle, not complete game equivalence. Limitations: No game compilation, dependency installation, launch, gameplay, hardware test or binary comparison was performed. Upstream claims remain separate from independently verified build flags. stellar7-apple2-iolo-reconstruction.title: Stellar 7 — Apple II lossless source and asset reconstruction

stellar7-apple2-iolo-reconstruction.status: Upstream exact native disk reconstruction; partial semantic and gameplay coverage
stellar7-apple2-iolo-reconstruction.notes: Identity: README and artifact provenance pin the supplied stella7.dsk and original manual. This repository maintains all 35 logical file representations, source and editable assets. README explicitly preserves original ownership and disclaims any implied redistribution license. Classification: Address-preserving ca65 game reconstruction plus lossless JSON assets and exact disk generation. The optional model viewer is an inspection aid; gameplay output remains the original Apple II program rather than a game-specific emulation wrapper. Source CPU: The recovered TITLE.2 decoder selects 6502 and contains native A/X/Y and zero-page operations. Other program/overlay files are reconstructed ca65 code; the launcher is Applesoft BASIC. Target CPU: The configured source uses .setcpu "6502" and the Makefile/README produce native Apple II disk images; host Python and Canvas model viewing do not establish another CPU target. Build: Upstream verification reports passing 17 tests, all 35 payload hashes, exact-image identity and a fresh second build. Apple2ts tests cover startup, menu, briefing, controls and a fixture-driven level transition; independent MAME reaches gameplay input. Those author-reported checks are preserved as evidence only. All four build flags remain unknown because this review did not independently build, compare or run the output. Limitations: Not rerun here. Full seven-system completion, save/high-score persistence, audio and joystick fidelity remain untested; Ctrl-R self-destruct is unresolved. Exact mode preserves original DOS/reserved/slack data, not reconstructed OS source. Runtime profiles: Upstream tests an Apple II+ configuration in MAME and a separate Apple2ts scenario, but does not establish minimum CPU/RAM requirements. These tested configurations are documented without inferring a minimum profile. AI: Commit 60dadd0 explicitly attributes the recovery to "single turn disassembly by astra"; status notes refer to installed Codex skills. AI usage is evidenced, but no interface label is inferred from the model-name attribution, so tools stays empty. Relationships: Distinct from the already tracked Andy McFadden SourceGen project: that project covers the official/4am release with an early ROCK3 loader, whereas this supplied disk includes an added TITLE.2 and different payload layout. Inspected bootstrap.py/recover.py generate ca65 source directly from assets/raw binaries with their own control-flow renderer and no SourceGen import. The root is non-fork; no borrowed SourceGen source is credited. This supports an independent reconstruction, not a format-converted mirror. thames-isis-cli-runner.notes: Mark Ogden’s maintained Thames source explicitly derives from John Elliott’s Thames 0.1.1. Elliott’s official page identifies an ISIS-II runner for the tools used to build CP/M3, and the maintained loader/interpreter confirm direct original-binary execution. Count the original tarball and enhanced fork as one lineage under ogdenpm/thames-src. CP/M3 is the build product of example guest tools, not the OS API being emulated. Inspected default-branch head: dd545328888b6e989c5975053372d97a36dc336f. Modern tooling executes linked ISIS-II Intel OMF images, often without file extensions. isis_load accepts module/start/data/end records, loads bytes and rejects unresolved relocation/external/library records. main creates synthetic MDS BIOS/ISIS trap stubs in RAM, loads the argv-selected tool and enters the interpreter. ISIS OPEN/CLOSE/READ/WRITE/SEEK/LOAD translate to host files through device mapping; the path needs original tools/support files but no original boot ROM or booted ISIS OS. ISIS-II 8080/8085 binaries are the intended guest source. Ian Collier’s xz80 engine was reduced to 8080/8085 semantics by default; thames.h leaves Z80 disabled and documents an optional build switch. The VS Release|x64 project sets Z80 for thames.c only, not the z80.c interpreter unit; this is a configuration caveat, not evidence of universal Z80 compatibility. Source_cpu therefore records 8080 and 8085, preserving optional Z80 ancestry in notes. The Visual Studio project explicitly has Win32 and x64 configurations and MachineX86 for Win32, supporting host x86 and x86-64 labels. Windows/Linux device paths and Unix usage are explicit in documentation. The CMake route is portable C but provides no further CPU guarantee. macOS is not asserted merely from Unix/CMake portability; guest 8080/8085 and code emitted by ASM48/ASM51/PLM80 are not host architectures. CMake >=3.5 builds the C sources and runs Perl Scripts/getVersion.pl to generate version headers; a checked-in VS solution/project is the alternative. Unix line endings matter to the version generator’s dirty-tree detection. The complete tree contains no GitHub Actions workflow. Documentation’s successful guest-tool lists are maintainer reports, not current-host build proof, and the per-file VS Z80 define needs review if enabling the optional mode. No build or guest test was attempted. All four build flags remain null: compilation, execution, gameplay and byte-equivalence are independently unverified. No numerical host RAM/CPU-generation floor or minimum OS release was established. The 64 KiB emulated address space and ISIS 6.3 filename limits are guest properties, while Windows SDK10/v143 are build settings rather than runtime minima. runtime_profiles remains empty. Partial ISIS.LAB/ISIS.DIR synthesis, less-tested CONSOLE/WHOCON/line-mode I/O, Enter-dependent keyboard handling and heuristic tool-error detection materially limit compatibility. The selected primary documentation, implementation/build/licence sources and latest 30 default-branch commit metadata contain no explicit affirmative development-AI attribution. ai.usage remains null with no tool names; absence is not proof of non-use. John Elliott origin and Mark Ogden enhancements remain one Thames family. The interpreter has GPL-2.0-or-later headers and COPYING is GPLv2; several ISIS/loader files have GNU Library GPL v2-or-later notices, so preserve mixed component terms. Original Intel tools are separately licensed. Documentation recommends newer native-C ports for several tools; those execute recompiled source and must not be conflated with Thames running originals. The original Odyssey 2/C64 ancestry is context, not a separately inspected code lineage in this batch. No root project-level LICENSE/COPYING grant was found in the complete tree or reviewed README. It loads original CP/M .COM/.CPM programs at 0x100 and runs Ian Collier’s Z80 interpreter, while wrappers such as zxc, zxas, zxlink, zxlibr and zxobjtohex adapt host arguments for existing compiler tools. Network device.c implements native SANA-II Amiga driver dispatch and hardware access; rtg/mntgfx-gcc.c implements graphics-card integration. README identifies the original MNT source and independent fork status, with firmware and ARM-side logic in separate repositories. Top-level build invokes pinned Amiga toolchain workflows; net/Makefile sets68020 and includes host-side test targets elsewhere in the suite. A reviewed code-fix commit explicitly credits Codex review; attribution is limited to review assistance. Requires ZZ9000 ZorroII/III hardware; ZZ9000AX audio and Picasso96/USB/network dependencies vary by component. Matched firmware/bitstream/SDK versions matter, especially ZorroII memory-layout negotiation; driver source alone does not provide a complete setup. The board’s ARM coprocessors are not the CPU executing the Amiga-side network driver; retain separate roles. No independent hardware/runtime/test execution; original MNT lineage is one family, not an extra project count. Maintained Amiga-side hardware driver source, not a reconstruction of a historical original binary. No source CPU is inferred from the modern hardware family. net/Makefile explicitly defaults to CPU=68020 and soft float. This records the inspected native network-driver target; other suite components can vary. The board ARM/FPGA firmware lives elsewhere and is not the Amiga driver CPU. Amiga-side m68k toolchain; inspected network component default 68020 and soft float. Board FPGA/ARM firmware separate from host driver CPU. penpen-ski-apple-ii-cobinee.status: Substantive game source reviewed; independent build and runtime unverified
penpen-ski-apple-ii-cobinee.notes: Identity: CoBinee’s skiing game presents a penguin on a scrolling course. game.s contains idle, start, play and game-over states; penpen.s handles left/right steering and sprite updates, with off-route failure and result display in the game loop. Classification: Native assembly homebrew, with a committed ski.dsk, source and sprite/tile assets. It is a game implementation rather than a graphics demonstration or a generic Apple II emulator. Source CPU: This is newly authored homebrew, with no recovered predecessor executable. No original-binary CPU or source language is assigned from the target machine; those source fields are intentionally empty. Target CPU: crt0.s, game.s and penpen.s explicitly select .setcpu "6502" and implement the native loop. The ca65/ld65 pipeline uses custom Apple II configuration; there is no evidence of a 65C02 or 65816 requirement. Build: The makefile assembles the six native modules with ca65, links with ld65/apple2.cfg and packages boot/app files using the included AppleCommander jar and an initial disk image. It expects object/output directories; its end-to-end prerequisites and resulting disk have not been validated. Limitations: No candidate compilation, testing, launch, gameplay or byte comparison was performed. All four independent build flags remain null. Runtime profiles: README documents left/right keys; source also accepts J/L and space to begin/restart. The reviewed game uses 7x8 masked/unmasked sprite/tile drawing and speaker tones. The packaging is a DOS-style binary disk workflow; an exact graphics resolution, numeric RAM floor, machine subtype or required OS version is not assigned from the limited renderer sample. AI: No explicit development-AI disclosure was found in the inspected README, implementation/build sample, any available rights files, and the first 6 available default-branch commit messages (request cap 20). This bounded negative result does not prove non-use. Gameplay logic, assistant filenames, and repository age are not attribution evidence. Relationships: One native skiing game in this repository. No LICENSE or explicit licensing declaration appears in the complete tree or inspected source. The bundled AppleCommander binary, DOS disk templates and art require their own provenance checks before redistribution. The normalized root, title/alias and lineage screen found no same-code project in the 1,833-project baseline or expanded 2,249-root prior-review union.
